messages.author: b7a2af1a9862973c
messages.subject: count reads in chromosomal region - featureCounts?
parts:
Hi,
I am interested in a region on human chromosome 11 (47,371,468 bp to 47,441,229 bp, length 69,762 bp). I have total RNA sequencing data on 500 individuals which have been aligned to the genome using STAR. There are very few annotated features in this region (four). I would like to know how many reads align to this region. How can I determine this, using the output files generated by STAR (sam.bam files)? Is there any way to use the featureCounts function?
Thanks, Ina

messages.author: bce99ba71cd48eea
messages.subject: Re: count reads in chromosomal region - featureCounts?
parts:
Yes, featureCounts can do it. Since you already have had the mapping results (ie the sam and/or bam files), and you have defined the target region (chr11, 47,371,468 bp to 47,441,229), you can first create a SAF format annotation file that contains only one line:

target chr11 47371468 47441229 +

, where the delimiter is <TAB>. Let's say the file name is my_annotation.SAF .

You can then run featureCounts like

$ featureCounts -a my_annotation.SAF -F SAF -o my_counts.txt -p -T 8 *.sam *.bam

This will generate a new file, my_counts.txt. If there are 500 individuals, I assume that you have 500 sam or bam files, so you will have 500 columns (plus 6 columns defining the target region) in this file, giving the counts of read-pairs in each sam or bam file that are mapped to the target region.

messages.author: bce99ba71cd48eea
messages.subject: Re: count reads in chromosomal region - featureCounts?
parts:
It appeared that you did strand-specific read assignment in both runs (strandSpecific = 2 : the reads are assigned to the genes that are on the opposite strand). Namely, when you assign reads to the region of interest defined in the SAF file, you only included the reads that were mapped to the negative strand (because the region of interest is on the positive strand). However, some of your four genes in the GTF file are on the positive strand but some are on negative strand, hence the set of reads assigned to the four genes is different to the set of reads assigned to the interest region. For example,  ENSG00000255197 is on negative strand, hence only the reads that are mapped to the positive strand are assigned to this gene.

Because you want to do strand-specific read assignment, and the four genes are on different strands, what is the number of reads you want to have in the region of interest? If you just want to have the total read number mapped to the region of interest disregarding their strands, you can remove the "strandSpecific" option from your first run (with SAF), but it will still be inconstant to your gene-level read assignment (with GTF file).

messages.author: bce99ba71cd48eea
messages.subject: Re: count reads in chromosomal region - featureCounts?
parts:
Hi Ina,

If my understanding is correct, you created two SAF files: one with all 100-bp buckets on the positive strand and the other with all buckets on the negative strand, then you use strandSpecific=2 to assign reads to either of these SAF files.

If you use strandSpecific=2, you can have strand-specific counting results (only reads mapped to the opposite strand of the buckets are counted). It is less straightforward than using strandSpecific=1 (counting reads that are mapped to the same strand of the buckets) but you can still work out the correct counts to either strands.

I'm not sure why it takes a very long time on the negative strand -- the speed should be similar on both strands, and it should be very fast (if you use like 16 threads). Does the counting result to the negative strand make sense?

Cheers,
Yang

messages.author: bce99ba71cd48eea
messages.subject: Re: count reads in chromosomal region - featureCounts?
parts:
Hi Ina,

If your reads are paired-end, the second read nearly always has an opposite strandness to the first read. If you turned on the paired-end mode in featureCounts, the second read is flipped to the opposite strand before strand-specific read assignment. Maybe this can explain the difference between the results from featureCounts and samtools.

Cheers,
Yang

messages.author: bce99ba71cd48eea
messages.subject: Re: count reads in chromosomal region - featureCounts?
parts:
Yes, you can define base positions as features in the SAF file. You may give all the features the same "gene name" or different "gene names" like

foo chr1 10000 10000 +
foo chr1 10001 10001 +
foo chr1 10002 10002 +
foo chr1 10003 10003 +
foo chr1 10004 10004 +
...
foo chr1 19999 19999 +
foo chr1 20000 20000 +

You then need to run featureCounts on the feature-level mode  (useMetaFeatures=FALSE) and allow multi-assignment of the reads (allowMultiOverlap = TRUE). This will give the number of reads mapped to each base location (ie, reads that have any mapped base at this base location) in your SAF file.

messages.author: bce99ba71cd48eea
messages.subject: Re: count reads in chromosomal region - featureCounts?
parts:
If you're doing single-base level read assignment, setting "largestOverlap=TRUE" is meaningless because all overlapping length is 1 bp between the read and each 1-bp "feature". It is suggested not using this parameter for single-base level read assignment because it makes the program slower.

The default value for "minOverlap" is 1.
